newsitem.title: UK: FKI to pay 131 mln stg for Bridon.
newsitem.headline: FKI to pay 131 mln stg for Bridon.

text.p: British engineering group FKI Plc said on Monday it made an agreed 131 million stg bid for wire rope and lifting systems maker Bridon Plc.
FKI will pay 175 pence per Bridon ordinary share, the companies said in a joint statement.
Bridon's share price of Bridon was already up 35 pence at 172-1/2p when the announcement was made on Monday.
The offer price represents premium of 65 percent to its mid-market price on June 27, the last trading before Bridon announced it was in talks with FKI on June 30.
FKI said it had purchased 22.32 million shares, representing 29.9 percent in Bridon at the offer price.
FKI's chairman Jeff Whalley said the acquisition was in line with FKI's strategy and was an "excellent fit" with its existing activities.
Brian Clayton, Bridon's chairman, described the merger as "sound industrial logic" and said it was unanimously recommending FKI's offer.
